subject: [PATCH v3 2/3] mm: swap: drop dropbehind swap cache folios on writeback completion

2026-08-18.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's swap management to drop PG_dropbehind folios from the swap cache immediately after writeback completion, rather than waiting for reclaim to find them later. This is achieved by introducing a new function, swap_writeback_dropbehind_folio(), which is called when writeback completes and frees the folios in batches. The patch also updates various functions to use this new function and adds necessary locking mechanisms to ensure thread safety. The goal of this change is to improve performance by reducing the time spent on reclaiming swap cache folios.

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Barry Song expressed confusion about the patch's restriction to only support non-LRU folios, wondering if this limitation prevents potential optimizations for madv_pageout and noted that zram might benefit from the patch in the future.

Reviewer Barry Song noted that file-backed folios in other filesystems and drivers also use workqueues to handle dropbehind, and suggested extending the patch to include them for consistency.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Alexandre,
Thanks very much for your patch!

I don't quite understand why we only support NON-LRU folios. Does this
restriction prevent potential optimizations for madv_pageout?

Also, zram might benefit from your patch in the future with
asynchronous hardware compression and software compression such as
kcompressd[1].

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20250430082651.3152444-1-qun-wei.lin@mediatek.com/

[...]

---

This is good. For file dropbehind, I see both F2FS [1] and block
devices [2] reinventing workqueues in their own filesystems or
drivers, while folio_end_dropbehind() simply benefits from its safe,
sleepable context. This seems a bit odd.

So I'm really curious whether this could be extended to file-backed
folios as well, so that those filesystems and device drivers don't
have to deal with this themselves.

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260820071438.695893-1-qiwenjie@xiaomi.com/
[2] https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260730-blk-dontcache-v7-2-3e8e6850068d@columbia.edu/

Thanks
Barry

reviews.author: Matthew Wilcox
reviews.summary: The reviewer suggests basing the current patch on a different series by Tal, citing that it would be easier to implement
reviews.raw_body:
You should probably both be aware of Tal's series:

https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20260730-blk-dontcache-v7-0-3e8e6850068d@columbia.edu/

In fact, I'd base this series on Tal's.  It would be considerably
easier.

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch improves the handling of swap cache folios by dropping them from their cache once writeback completes, rather than leaving them for reclaim to find later. This is achieved by adding a new function `swap_writeback_dropbehind_folio` that takes a folio as an argument and drops it from its cache after writeback has completed. The patch also updates several other functions to use this new function. The goal of the patch is to improve performance by reducing the number of times swap cache folios are scanned for reclaim, which can be expensive operations.

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Barry Song pointed out that the question he asked in a previous email about how the swap cache folios are handled when writeback completes has not been addressed, and requested an answer to this question.

Reviewer Barry Song suggested using a bio_in_atomic() helper to determine if bio completion should be moved to a workqueue, and proposed reusing Tal's code for this purpose.
